column1: depreciate§Do not depreciate a result just because it was easy to get.§不要因为一个结果得来容易就**贬低**它。
depreciatory§A depreciatory shrug can end a proposal faster than an argument.§一个**轻蔑**的耸肩比一场争论更快终结一项提案。
deprive§Sleep deprivation deprives you of judgment before energy.§睡眠不足先**夺走**判断力，然后才是精力。
derail§A single question derailed a presentation she had rehearsed for weeks.§一个问题就让她排练数周的演示**脱了轨**。
derelict§He was found derelict in his duty and quietly moved.§他被认定**玩忽职守**，随后被悄悄调离。
deride§It costs nothing to deride a plan and everything to make one.§**嘲笑**一个计划不花什么，做出一个计划却要付出一切。
derivative§Cream is a derivative of milk and behaves quite differently.§奶油是牛奶的**衍生物**，性质却大不相同。
derive§She derives more pleasure from the index than from the text.§她从索引中**得到**的乐趣比正文还多。
derogate§The clause does not derogate from any existing right.§该条款**不减损**任何现有权利。
descend§The family descends from a clerk who could not write.§这个家族的**祖先**是一位不会写字的书吏。
descriptive§Descriptive grammar records what people say, not what they should.§**描写语法**记录人们怎么说，而不是应该怎么说。
desecration§Painting over the mural was a kind of desecration.§把壁画涂掉是一种**亵渎**。
deserter§Deserters were pardoned in 1919 and named in 2006.§**逃兵**在一九一九年获赦，在二〇〇六年才被列出姓名。
designate§He was designated to speak and said nothing for an hour.§他被**指定**发言，却一小时没说一句话。
desirability§The desirability of the post fell when the travel was cut.§取消差旅后，这个职位的**吸引力**下降了。
desolate§She felt desolate for a week and then began again.§她**消沉**了一周，然后重新开始。
despair§Despair is a poor guide and an accurate barometer.§**绝望**是糟糕的向导，却是准确的晴雨表。
despise§He despised the prize and kept it on the shelf.§他**鄙视**这个奖，却把它摆在架子上。
despoil§Collectors despoiled the site long before archaeologists arrived.§早在考古学家到来之前，收藏者就已把遗址**洗劫一空**。
despondency§Despondency after a rejection lasts about as long as you let it.§被拒后的**沮丧**持续多久，取决于你让它持续多久。
destruction§Destruction of the records was the only order that was obeyed.§**销毁**记录是唯一被执行的命令。
detachment§A detachment of twenty was sent ahead to the pass.§一支二十人的**分遣队**被派往山口。
deterrent§The penalty is a deterrent only if it is enforced.§罚则只有在被执行时才有**威慑**力。
detest§She detested the phrase and used it anyway.§她**厌恶**这个说法，却还是用了。
detractor§His detractors and admirers agree on the facts and nothing else.§**贬低他的人**和欣赏他的人只在事实上一致，别的都不一致。
detrimental§Working through lunch is detrimental to the afternoon.§午饭时间还在工作，对下午**有害**。
devastate§The news devastated a family that had prepared for it.§这个消息**击垮**了一个早有准备的家庭。
devious§There is nothing devious about asking a direct question.§直接提问没有什么**迂回**可言。
devoid§A room devoid of clutter is not the same as a tidy one.§一个**没有杂物**的房间与一个整洁的房间不是一回事。
dexterous§Dexterous hands made the repair; a patient eye found the crack.§**灵巧的**手完成了修补，耐心的眼睛发现了裂缝。
diagnose§The fault was diagnosed by listening, not by measuring.§这个故障是**靠听出来**的，不是靠测出来的。
diagnostic§A diagnostic run takes four minutes and saves four hours.§一次**诊断**运行要四分钟，能省下四小时。
diaphanous§The wing is diaphanous and stronger than it looks.§这只翅膀**薄如蝉翼**，却比看上去结实。
diatribe§A diatribe persuades the people who already agreed.§**激烈的抨击**只能说服本来就赞同的人。
dichotomy§The dichotomy between amateur and professional was invented quite late.§业余与专业的**二分法**是相当晚才被发明的。
dictator§The dictator's statue outlasted his government by forty years.§这位**独裁者**的雕像比他的政权多存在了四十年。
diction§Poetic diction of the period admits no ordinary word.§那个时期的诗歌**用语**不容许任何日常词汇。
dictum§Her dictum was that no draft should be shown before Thursday.§她的**原则**是周四之前不给任何人看草稿。
didactic§A didactic tone in a museum label loses the visitor.§博物馆说明牌上的**说教**语气会赶走观众。
diffidence§Diffidence cost her a job she was better suited to than anyone.§**羞怯**让她失去了一份最适合她的工作。
diffident§He is diffident in person and forceful on paper.§他当面**腼腆**，落笔却有力。
diffuse§Responsibility was so diffuse that nobody could be asked.§责任**分散**得没有任何人可以被问责。
dignify§A proper title dignifies work that was previously unpaid.§一个正式的头衔让原本无偿的工作**有了体面**。
digress§If I may digress for one sentence, the date is also wrong.§容我**离题**一句，那个日期也是错的。
digression§What looks like a digression turns out to be the argument.§看似**离题**的部分，最后才是论点所在。
dilatory§A dilatory response is itself an answer.§**拖延**的回应本身就是一种回答。
dilettante§There is nothing wrong with being a dilettante if you say so.§只要自己承认，做个**业余爱好者**并无不妥。
diligence§Due diligence turned up a lease nobody had mentioned.§**尽职调查**查出了一份无人提及的租约。
diligent§Diligent copying preserved a text the original lost.§**勤勉的**抄录保存下了原本已失传的文本。
diminish§Nothing diminishes a good idea like a bad first slide.§没有什么比糟糕的第一张幻灯片更能**贬损**一个好想法。
diminutive§"Booklet" is a diminutive and sounds like one.§booklet 是个**指小**词，听起来也确实如此。
dire§The consequences were dire for everyone except the people who decided.§后果对所有人都**很严重**，唯独对作决定的人不然。
dirge§The tune began as a dance and ended up a dirge.§这支曲子起初是舞曲，最后成了**挽歌**。
disaffect§Disaffected members left quietly and took their records with them.§**心生不满**的成员悄悄离开，还带走了自己的资料。
disarm§The country disarmed on paper and rearmed within a decade.§这个国家在纸面上**裁军**，十年内就重新武装。
disavow§He disavowed the translation but not the fee.§他**否认**了那份译稿，却没有退回稿酬。
discard§Do not discard the envelope; the postmark dates the letter.§**别丢掉**信封，邮戳标明了信件的日期。
discern§At that distance you can discern the tower but not the clock.§在那个距离能**辨出**塔楼，却看不清钟。
discernment§Discernment is what remains after taste has been examined.§**眼力**是品味经过检验之后留下来的东西。
discharge§The river discharges into the estuary through four channels.§这条河经由四条水道**注入**河口湾。
discipline§Archaeology became a discipline only in the last century.§考古学到上个世纪才成为一门**学科**。
disclaimer§The disclaimer was longer than the recipe.§**免责声明**比食谱还长。
disclose§He disclosed the conflict of interest before anyone asked.§在有人问起之前，他就主动**披露**了利益冲突。
disclosure§Full disclosure ended the speculation in a single afternoon.§全面**披露**一个下午就结束了猜测。
discomfit§Nothing discomfits a speaker like a room that will not laugh.§没有什么比一个不肯笑的会场更让讲话者**狼狈**。
disconnect§Disconnect the battery before you touch anything else.§碰其他部件之前先**断开**电池。
